newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Bids for Tabaqueira worth up to $236 million.
newsitem.headline: Bids for Tabaqueira worth up to $236 million.

text.p: Portuguese, Spanish, French and U.S. groups bid for Portuguese state-owned cigarette manufacturer Tabaqueira valuing the 65 percent stake for sale at up to $236 million, officials said on Tuesday.

The three bids were: 5,610 escudos ($36.43) per share offered by Portugal's Empresa Madeirense de Tabacos in partnership with Spanish company Tabacalera; 5,100 escudos per share offered by Portugal's Jorge de Mello industrial group in partnership with U.S. company Philip Morris; and 4,800 escudos per share offered by French company Seita.

The bid by EMT/Tabacalera is worth 36.465 billion escudos ($236 million), the bid by Jorge de Mello/Philip Morris is worth 33.15 billion escudos ($215 million) and Seita's offer is worth 31.2 billion escudos ($202 million).

The Socialist government of Prime Minister Antonio Guterres, which plans to sell the stake by public competition at a minimum price of 4,650 escudos ($30) per share, had said it expected to raise more than 32 billion escudos ($207 million).
The winner of the public competition is expected to be known next month, officials said.
The jury will consider factors such as the financial strength of the bidders, their experience and their strategic plans for Tabaqueira, they said.
Tabaqueira has a dominant share of the Portuguese tobacco market. ($1=154.0 Escudo)
